title: China-to-Rwanda Lithium Battery & Power Bank Compliance Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.target_requirement: Rwanda imports of lithium batteries and power banks are controlled through Rwanda Standards Board (RSB) processes rather than one dedicated battery statute. In-scope products usually require Product Verification of Conformity (PVoC), a Certificate of Conformity, and import inspection. For selected regulated items, S-Mark conditions can also apply. The country uses RS standards with IEC-derived references, and electrical context is 230 V / 50 Hz.
target_standards: Rwandan Standards Board (RSB) import-product verification procedures
RSB Certificate of Conformity process for regulated electrical goods
RS import inspection framework for selected categories
RSB S-Mark conditions (where listed by product category)
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/GB-T baselines for battery product safety, with CCC requirements in applicable domestic categories. These are domestic regimes and do not match the Rwanda-specific importer-led PVoC and CoC release model in structure.
china_standards: GB 31241-2022 — Safety requirements for portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries
GB/T portable battery and charger-related safety references
China Compulsory Certification (CCC) catalogue where applicable
rows.gap: Rwanda creates a destination-level compliance layer through PVoC, CoC, and import inspection. Rwanda does not run EU-style horizontal regimes in this lane, so requirements such as RoHS and EU-style battery passport/outdoor-noise sets are not the mapping target.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for in-scope regulated imports, with PVoC, Certificate of Conformity, and import inspection generally required before market entry.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for Chinese domestic process in applicable domestic categories, but the specific Rwanda PVoC/CoC importer-led model is not equivalent.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] The key Rwanda target-side requirement is document-led regulatory entry through the importer, not replacement of Chinese domestic certification alone. CN GB/GB-T remains useful as technical baseline only.

rows.requirement: Cell and battery pack safety basis
rows.target_requirement: For Rwanda entry, import files for lithium cells and power banks normally reference RS safety documentation and IEC-aligned test logic (RS/IEC family references). Practical evidence is expected on protection, abuse resistance, and failure behavior as part of PVoC and import compliance.
target_standards: RS-adopted IEC 62133-series requirements for portable rechargeable lithium cells and batteries
RSB safety documentation expectations for imported battery packs
rows.china_equivalent: China applies GB 31241-2022 and related references such as GB/T 18287 for domestic battery safety. These are useful for design engineering but not a direct destination substitute for Rwanda entry conditions.
china_standards: GB 31241-2022 — Safety requirements for portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries
GB/T 18287 family references for lithium battery technology
rows.gap: The technical test baseline is not the same as the target-market paperwork model. Rwanda entry depends on RSB-aligned import documentation even when GB/GB-T safety testing already exists.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory to provide safety-aligned technical evidence in the import-file package for regulated categories.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in Chinese domestic market safety management for applicable categories, but not structured as Rwanda-style destination import conformity proof.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Use IEC/RS-aligned safety evidence for Rwanda filings and map each report to PVoC import obligations; Chinese GB tests help reduce technical risk but do not replace destination compliance packaging.

rows.target_requirement: Rwanda importers should ensure power banks with wireless functions align with local wireless regulation expectations through RURA and include the related evidence in RSB compliance dossiers. EMC and electrical safety claims in the dossier should support the import inspection outcome.
target_standards: RURA requirements for radio/telecom capable consumer electronics
RSB conformity expectations for EMC and equipment documentation
rows.china_equivalent: China relies on GB/T EMC test methods and SRRC for domestic radio approval pathways. These references are useful but frequency allocation and radio-control logic are not automatically transferable to Rwanda import evidence.
rows.gap: The gap is usually evidence scope and destination mapping, especially where RURA expects local telecom/wireless interpretation and the importer is responsible for file consistency.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for wireless-capable imports that fall under Rwanda’s telecom/wireless inspection expectations.
mandatory_status.cn: Domestic Chinese approvals (GB/T, SRRC) are mandatory where applicable in China but do not directly replace Rwanda's RURA-aligned entry expectations.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat RURA mapping as destination mandatory evidence for wireless models. Chinese GB/T and SRRC evidence is supportive but must be translated into the Rwanda importer’s compliance set.

rows.requirement: Rwanda market access via local importer
rows.target_requirement: Rwanda market access is usually executed with a local importer and requires PVoC, Certificate of Conformity, and import inspection for controlled products. Logistics are frequently routed through Mombasa or Dar es Salaam before overland entry into Rwanda.
target_standards: RSB import inspection process for regulated goods
RRA-linked customs filing references for PVoC and CoC
Regional route governance for Mombasa and Dar es Salaam trans-shipment
rows.china_equivalent: China uses CCC and domestic regulatory checks where applicable, but these do not create an equivalent Rwanda in-country importer release model; importer responsibility and pre-clearance flow differ.
rows.gap: A strong compliance chain in China does not remove the need for Rwanda destination release evidence and importer handling. EU-style horizontal obligations such as RoHS, battery passport programs, and outdoor-noise packages are not in this lane.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for regulated imports before customs release in Rwanda.
mandatory_status.cn: Domestic Chinese compliance is mandatory for China market and export formalities, not a direct substitute for Rwanda importer-led release.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Allocate compliance scope by market first: CN baseline controls plus separate Rwanda import-control chain through a local importer (PVoC, CoC, import inspection) is mandatory in practice.

source.publisher: Rwanda Revenue Authority and linked import controls

rows.target_requirement: UN 38.3 remains a mandatory technical basis for lithium battery transport. For Rwanda, logistics must also account for corridor reality: most consignments pass through Mombasa or Dar es Salaam before Rwanda land entry, so transport documents and consignee/importer readiness are key.
target_standards: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III Section 38.3
IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations for air shipments
Dangerous-goods handling references for road/sea segments
rows.china_equivalent: China typically requires UN 38.3 for lithium batteries and follows CAAC/ICAO and domestic transport rules by mode. This does not remove Rwanda-side corridor and importer clearance requirements.
china_standards: CAAC/ICAO dangerous goods framework for air
GB 12268 and JT/T 617 for domestic transport in China
rows.gap: Rwanda-specific gap is mostly logistics-administration: corridor documents, importer handoff completeness, and harmonised declaration content for landed consignments. The safety test base is commonly present in China exports already.

mandatory_status.target: UN 38.3 is mandatory in practice for internationally accepted battery transport; route/clearance administration via transit corridors is mandatory for Rwanda entry.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for relevant transport modes under Chinese dangerous-goods and aviation requirements for lithium exports.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep UN 38.3 documentation and route-specific logistics evidence synchronized. In practice, Rwanda entry often fails on paper trail and importer handover points before it fails on raw transport testing.
